newsitem.title: GERMANY: FDP denies report it wants to raise German debt.
newsitem.headline: FDP denies report it wants to raise German debt.

text.p: Germany's Free Democratic Party (FDP), junior coalition partner with Chancellor Helmut Kohl, denied a report on Friday that it wanted 20 billion marks in new debt to plug Germany's budget deficit.

An FDP spokesman in Bonn said the report in the Bild newspaper that said the FDP favoured the new debt instead of raising taxes as Bonn seeks to shore up its finances in 1997, the key year to meet entry criteria for European monetary union (EMU), was wrong and fabricated.

The parliamentary panel of the FDP, which has said it would oppose any tax increase proposed by Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), has approved the proposal even though it would put Germany's deficit at 3.2 percent in 1997, the newspaper said.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel reaffirmed late on Thursday his strict interpretation of the deficit criteria in the Maastricht Treaty, which he said calls for a budget deficit of 3.0 percent or less.
But FDP parliamentary leader Hermann Otto Solms told the newspaper that he did not believe 3.2 percent would be problematic in Germany qualifying for currency union.
"We have never set ourselves upon this level," he said of Waigel's interprepation of the treaty as saying 3.0 percent in the newspaper. "The euro can still legally be achieved."
